title: Adding one simplex to a simplicial set is a pushout along the boundary of the standard simplex
statement: Let $U\subseteq V$ be a simplicial subset of a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $n\geq0$ let $\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial set with $\Delta[n]_m$ the set of order-preserving maps $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ and $\Delta[n](\psi)(\varphi)=\varphi\circ\psi$, and let $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial subset whose $m$-simplices are the non-surjective $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ (so $\partial\Delta[0]$ is empty). Suppose $n\geq0$ and $x\in V_n$ with $x\notin U_n$ satisfy (1) $V_i=U_i$ for $i<n$, (2) $V_n=U_n\cup\{x\}$, and (3) every $z\in V_j$ with $j>n$ and $z\notin U_j$ is degenerate. Let $a:\Delta[n]\to V$ be the morphism of simplicial sets $a(\varphi)=V(\varphi)(x)$ for $\varphi\in\Delta[n]_m$. Then $a(\partial\Delta[n]_m)\subseteq U_m$ for every $m$, and, writing $b:\partial\Delta[n]\to U$ for the restriction of $a$, the commutative square formed by $b$, $a$ and the inclusions $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$, $U\subseteq V$ is a pushout square of simplicial sets: for every simplicial set $Y$ and morphisms $g:U\to Y$, $h:\Delta[n]\to Y$ with $g\circ b=h|_{\partial\Delta[n]}$ there is a unique morphism $f:V\to Y$ with $f|_U=g$ and $f\circ a=h$. (For $n=0$ the compatibility condition is empty, so $V$ with the inclusion of $U$ and $a$ is a coproduct $U\amalg\Delta[0]$.)

proof.text: The simplex $x$ is nondegenerate: if $x=V(\sigma)(y)$ for a map $\sigma:[n]\to[r]$ with $r<n$, then $y\in V_r=U_r$, so simplicial stability of $U$ would give $x\in U_n$. For $n=0$ there are no non-surjective maps to $[0]$. For $n>0$, if $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ is not surjective, choose $i$ outside its image and factor $\varphi=\delta_i\circ\psi$ by [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization]. The face $V(\delta_i)(x)$ lies in $V_{n-1}=U_{n-1}$, hence $a(\varphi)=U(\psi)(V(\delta_i)(x))\in U_m$. This defines $b$ and makes the square commute.

source.place: Lemma 018R (lemma-glue-simplex), statement and proof, the sentence 'Since clearly x is nondegenerate'; Lemma 0166 (lemma-face-degeneracy), proof of factorization through a missing face

proof.text: Every $z\in V_j\setminus U_j$ has a unique expression $z=V(\sigma)(x)$ for a surjective $\sigma:[j]\to[n]$. Indeed, apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] to $z$. Its nondegenerate ancestor $y$ is outside $U$ (otherwise $z\in U$); it cannot have degree below $n$ by (1), nor above $n$ by (3), and by (2) it is $x$ in degree $n$. Conversely, if $\sigma$ is surjective and $V(\sigma)(x)\in U_j$, choose an order-preserving section $\tau:[n]\to[j]$ of $\sigma$. Then $x=V(\tau)(V(\sigma)(x))\in U_n$, a contradiction. Thus the simplices outside $U$ are exactly the distinct surjective degeneracies of $x$.

source.place: Lemma 018R (lemma-glue-simplex), proof, induction showing every new simplex is a degeneracy of x and injectivity via Lemma 017S; Lemma 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets) supplies uniqueness

proof.text: Let $g:U\to Y$ and $h:\Delta[n]\to Y$ agree on the boundary. Define $f_j:V_j\to Y_j$ by $f_j(z)=g_j(z)$ for $z\in U_j$, and $f_j(V(\sigma)(x))=h_j(\sigma)$ for the unique surjection $\sigma:[j]\to[n]$ of step 2. To check naturality for $\theta:[k]\to[j]$, it is immediate for $z\in U_j$. For $z=V(\sigma)(x)$ outside $U$, write $\rho=\sigma\circ\theta$. If $\rho$ is surjective, step 2 gives $V(\theta)(z)=V(\rho)(x)$ outside $U$ and both sides of naturality equal $h_k(\rho)$. If $\rho$ is not surjective, step 1 puts $V(\theta)(z)=b_k(\rho)$ in $U_k$ and the boundary agreement gives $g_k(b_k(\rho))=h_k(\rho)=Y(\theta)(h_j(\sigma))$. Thus $f$ is a simplicial morphism extending $g$.

source.place: Lemma 018R (lemma-glue-simplex), proof, degreewise bijectivity of the pushout map; expanded here into the universal-property construction using the unique splitting of Lemma 017R

proof.text: For $\varphi:[j]\to[n]$, if $\varphi$ is surjective then $a_j(\varphi)$ lies outside $U$ by step 2 and $f_j(a_j(\varphi))=h_j(\varphi)$. Otherwise it lies on the boundary by step 1 and $f_j(a_j(\varphi))=g_j(b_j(\varphi))=h_j(\varphi)$. Hence $f\circ a=h$. Any other morphism with these restrictions agrees with $f$ on $U$, and on a new simplex $V(\sigma)(x)$ it must take the value $Y(\sigma)(h_n(\mathrm{id}_{[n]}))=h_j(\sigma)$; it is therefore $f$. This is the pushout universal property. When $n=0$, every map $[j]\to[0]$ is surjective and $\partial\Delta[0]$ is empty, so the same argument says $V=U\amalg\Delta[0]$.
